Test "Safety vs Energy Efficiency Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated product offers. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two message conditions: Safety Condition (emphasizes safety-critical, reliable residential HVAC control) or Energy Condition (emphasizes energy‑efficiency and cost savings). Both conditions present a Belimo residential control system at a fixed price point. Participants indicate purchase intent (1‑10 scale) and maximum price they would pay.. Sample: 500 U.S. homeowners (250 per condition) recruited via an online panel, balanced for age, income, and home ownership status.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1‑10) and maximum price willingness to pay for each condition.. Predictions: T1: Safety Condition will generate higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than Energy Condition.; T2: Energy Condition will generate higher purchase intent and higher willingness to pay than Safety Condition.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent in the Safety Condition is at least 10 points higher than in the Energy Condition (i.e., Safety ≥ Energy + 10), we conclude T1 is supported. If the difference is less than 10 points, we conclude neither theory is strongly supported. If the difference is less than €10, we conclude no significant difference and recommend further market research.. Cost: 2000 euros, 4 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes safety-critical, reliable residential HVAC control, leveraging Belimo’s commercial reputation for durability and technical excellence. Begin with a limited pilot offering through retail partners to test homeowner willingness to pay a premium for safety messaging. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: Simulated evidence SYN-D concerns a warehouse label printer and packing errors, which does not address homeowner motivations for safety-critical features or willingness to pay a premium for them. Therefore it does not affect T1. New claim: Homeowners will adopt a differentiated Belimo consumer proposition if they perceive it as a safety-critical, reliable solution for their home HVAC system, because they trust Belimo's reputation for durability and technical excellence in commercial applications.. Evidence: SYN-D.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that emphasizes safety-critical, reliable residential HVAC control, leveraging Belimo’s commercial reputation for durability and technical excellence. Begin with a limited pilot offering through retail partners to test homeowner willingness to pay a premium for safety messaging. Target customer: Homeowners who prioritize safety and reliability in their HVAC control system, particularly those who are risk‑averse and prefer brands with a proven track record in commercial applications.. Value proposition: A Belimo residential control system marketed as a safety‑critical, reliable solution that builds on the brand’s existing reputation for durability and technical excellence, offering peace of mind and reduced perceived risk of failure.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Safety vs Energy Efficiency Messaging Test (500 U.S. homeowners, two message conditions, purchase intent and price willingness) to quantify the premium homeowners are willing to pay for safety messaging.. Uncertainty: The size of the consumer market for Belimo and the actual willingness to pay a premium for safety‑critical features remain uncertain. The test will provide data to resolve this uncertainty.. Would change if: If the test shows the Energy Condition generates significantly higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than the Safety Condition, we would shift focus to energy‑efficiency messaging and consider a different consumer proposition.; If the test shows no significant difference between the two conditions, we would recommend further market research to better understand homeowner motivations and the size of the consumer market.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

Test "Residential Product Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized product exposure and willingness-to-pay (WTP) questions.. Sample: 500 U.S. homeowners (ages 25-55) who have considered purchasing a new HVAC control product in the past 12 months, recruited via an online panel.. Measure: 1) Purchase intent: binary (will buy) or intent to purchase within 12 weeks. 2) WTP: maximum price a respondent would pay for a Belimo residential zone damper. 3) Messaging preference: ranking Belimo vs. competitor on energy efficiency, durability, and brand prestige.. Predictions: T1: At least 20% of respondents will express purchase intent and indicate a WTP at least 10% above the competitor's average WTP, with higher energy-efficiency and durability rankings.; T2: At least 15% of respondents will express purchase intent and indicate a WTP at least 10% above the competitor's average WTP, with higher brand prestige and status rankings.. Decision rule: If purchase intent >=20% AND (Belimo WTP >= competitor WTP + 10% OR Belimo prestige ranking >= competitor prestige ranking), proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition. If purchase intent <20% OR Belimo WTP < competitor WTP - 10%, do not invest in a consumer proposition. If both conditions fail, maintain B2B focus.. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

DANBURY, Conn. — Belimo Americas, a manufacturer of damper actuators and control valves for commercial HVAC, announced the availability of products for residential applications with select actuators, round damper assemblies, and pressure bypass damper controls.

Total revenue for 2025 is expected to be USD 33.3 million dollar with 7% growth in the Business segment and 21% growth in the Pro segment, while Consumer revenues decreased 20% following the strategic decision to prioritize margin improvement.

Gross profit grew year-on-year in the Business and Pro segments, while gross profit in the Consumer segment was impacted negatively by a weakening US consumer sentiment, US tariffs and costs related to promotions and campaigns with key retail partners.

Belimo is a global market leader in the development, production, and sales of field devices for the energy-efficient control of heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems. The focus of its core business is on damper actuators, control valves, sensors and meters.

With an emphasis on product quality, durability with minimal maintenance, and highly innovative, technically advanced solutions, the Company has become a preferred choice in high-performance applications in large commercial buildings such as data centers, hospitals, schools and universities, offices, governmental buildings, infrastructure and industrial sites.

Belimo collaborates closely with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) of HVAC systems and system integrators who incorporate Belimo products into large-scale HVAC projects. It provides them with extensive technical support, including planning, customization, calibration, and troubleshooting – and conducts training for HVAC professionals to optimize installation effectiveness.
The company’s first product launch of 2020 offers HVAC contractors reliable, high-quality solutions with precise performance and offers the value-conscious homeowner a wider range of options.
In addition to our growing portfolio of DIY solutions sold through top retail and e-commerce channels, the majority of our technologies are installed by professionals.
